_comment: Loss profiles are data, not code, because there is no single right way to
weigh 'closer'. Published work on iterative sound-matching finds no loss
universally best, so the weights that decide which preset wins have to be
tunable without editing a comparison function. Add a profile; do not add a
special case to compare.py.
weights: how much each objective dimension counts towards the scalar an
optimiser minimises. A dimension that cannot be measured from the material
drops out and the rest are renormalised, so a missing feature never scores
as a perfect match.
scales: what counts as one unit of wrong, in the field's own units. A 3 dB
band error and a 20 ms attack error are both 1.0 under 'unpaired-v1'.
These come from what the plugin's own controls are worth: M0 measured
single Morgan switches moving bands by 1 to 5 dB.
residual is the one dimension the caller has to supply, from
analysis.align.residual_db, because a fingerprint does not keep the
waveform. It is weighted zero under 'unpaired-v1': subtracting a commercial
master from a render measures the difference between two performances.
residual_floor_db is where a correct answer bottoms out rather than zero --
M0 measured two renders of identical parameters differing by about -17 dB,
so anything below that is the plugin's own per-render variation.

unpaired-v1.description: A commercial recording against a render. Different performance, different notes, so only playing-invariant statistics are trusted.

paired-v1.description: The same DI through both sides. The performance is identical, so envelope and time-domain features mean what they say and are weighted up.
